To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
after coronary occlusion, S-T elevation and tension decrease and K+/Na+ increases.

after reperfusion, the S-T segment abnormality decreased in all experiments, despite the appearance of a new Q-wave in more than half these studies concomitantly with either a decrease, or no change, in contractile ability, and continuing myocardial potassium ion (K+) loss and sodium ion (Na+) accumulation.

(a) S-T segment mapping of epicardial ECGs is of limited value in quantitating myocardial infarction; (b) the S-T segment elevation is due to a "washout phenomenon" and (c) reperfusion does not reverse the biochemical changes that occur after coronary artery occlusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an experimental method for quantifying the size of myocardial infarcts.
the development of an experimental model for the study of acute myocardial ischemia.
the development of an experimental model of the ischemic heart which can be used to test the efficacy of various drugs on the heart.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
S-T segment elevation is a very poor indicator of infarct size, and that S-T segment mapping has little value in assessing the effectiveness of reperfusion.
the S-T segment changes are a function of the balance of the washout and the wash-in phenomena.
the S-T segment elevation is a marker of the extent of the area of myocardium that was ischemic, not of the amount of myocardium that is necrotic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the S-T segment elevation is a function of the washout of potassium ion from the ischemic zone and not a function of the extent of the necrotic area.
S-T segment mapping is of little or no value in assessing the efficacy of reperfusion.
the changes in the S.T. segment after coronary occlusion is a result of the changes in the K+/ Na+ ratio and the changes in tension is a result of changes in the K+ concentration.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the changes in S-T elevation that occur during acute myocardial ischemia and reperfusion are not a reliable indicator of the degree of myocardial necrosis and are likely to be the result of a washout of potassium from the ischemic myocardium during reperfusion.

S-T segment mapping may not be the best way to assess the effect of revascularization on infarcted myocardium, as it is not clear how much the S-T segment changes are related to the amount of myocardium at risk.
the S-T segment changes are not a good marker for infarct size.
